result.title: Why Bother Me Again? Benchmarking Personal Agent Memory for Interaction Preferences
result.summary: Personal intelligence systems are taking on increasingly complex everyday tasks, yet repeated questions, unnecessary confirmations, and unwanted outreach can turn capable assistance into interaction burden. Reducing this burden requires agents to remember how users want to be assisted. However, existing memory benchmarks focus on factual recall and personalized answers and rarely test how agents learn and act on interaction preferences. We introduce MemPABench, an interactive environment for on-policy evaluation of memory in personal agents. MemPABench poses long-horizon tasks requiring agents to decide when to clarify, confirm, or act autonomously. Four grounded simulated users hold 14 preferences across work and personal contexts. Their feedback spans 99 sessions over four months, with five event-driven changes per user testing memory updates. We evaluate preference selection, delivered behavior, and sensitivity to context and preference change. Evaluating four memory systems across four LLM backbones, we find that current memory brings limited gains in preference selection. Retrieval-based systems (i.e. Mem0, MemOS, simple RAG) do not outperform No Memory, while File-based memory improves accuracy but applies preferences beyond relevant contexts. Our analysis shows that current memory struggles to retrieve interaction preferences and adapt to preference changes. Even with the correct preference available, overriding the agent's default interaction habits remains challenging. The environment and dataset are available at https://mempabench.com.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 MemPABench 交互式基准，用四个模拟用户、99 段会话与事件驱动的偏好变化，评估个人智能体能否记住并依用户交互偏好决定何时澄清、确认或自主行动。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文虽不涉及视觉，但其「何时澄清、何时自主行动」的决策与偏好变化下的状态更新和停止判断，可能为 LVR 中 STOP 决策、持久化内部状态及证据获取的评价设计提供启发，具体迁移方式可供核查。
